title: Production startup does not fail closed on development secrets or insecure runtime configuration

original_titles.title: Default JWT secret baked into code; no *_FILE secret support and no boot-time override check
No startup guard against production running on dev-default secrets/DB URLs
Default JWT secret and dev DB credentials ship in code with no production fail-fast
Hardcoded dev credentials in seed and helper scripts
Access tokens use HS256 instead of the specified EdDSA/Ed25519
No kid claim in access tokens
Refresh-successor encryption key derived from the JWT secret

problem: config.py contains a public development JWT secret and development DB connection strings. The application startup does not reject production if the JWT secret or DB credentials remain default. There is no *_FILE secret loading. HS256 is used rather than the specified EdDSA/Ed25519, and refresh successor encryption derives from the JWT secret.
impact: A deployment with incomplete environment configuration could accept a known signing secret, and rotating JWT secrets also affects refresh-token successor encryption. Dev seed/helper credentials can be accidentally reused outside test environments.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Add a validated production settings model: reject known dev JWT secret, development DB password/host, missing TLS/cookie requirements, localhost origins and debug docs on production startup.
Implement *_FILE loading for signing keys, DB credentials, encryption keys and object-storage secrets; support mounted secrets without placing values in images or logs.

Separate JWT signing and refresh-successor encryption keys. Use key ids and a rotation plan. If EdDSA is required by the locked spec, migrate algorithm and token verifier with a bounded compatibility window.
Mark seed/helper scripts as development-only and make destructive reset require an explicit non-production database profile; reject production connection strings.
Add startup tests for missing/default secrets, valid production config, key rotation and accidental production seed invocation.

acceptance_criteria: JWT and refresh encryption use separate rotated secrets.
No secret value is emitted in logs, env examples, build artifacts or commits.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
